verified_against_binary: v2.37.6 removes a retraction that was doing no work for a reader, and makes the placement rule enforceable. Three retraction notes existed in two different fields. Sorted by what they actually do for someone reading now: paths.session-paths-denied's is PROTECTIVE and correctly in caveats -- the withdrawn advice was 'retry', which would loop forever against a deterministic denial, so a reader who followed it needs telling. plugins.hooks-do-fire's corrected a belief a reader can arrive holding independently ('hooks are disabled in Cowork'), which is content rather than release history; it is reworded to address the belief instead of our old text. shell.no-package-installs' corrected only our own previous wording, and explained the reasoning failure while doing it -- 'that was an inference from the network constraints'. It told a reader nothing they could act on, because the rewritten guidance already says user-scoped installs work. Removed; the changelog is where release history belongs. New validator rule rejects retraction phrasing in `detail` while allowing it in `caveats`, checked against the exact sentence that prompted this plus three legitimate forms.
note: Open, and not addressed: retraction notes have no lifecycle. The one remaining in caveats will sit there indefinitely, long after nobody could still be acting on the advice it withdraws. There is no mechanism to expire one.
